regressions.cause: reading a row's fields without assuming its shape. Measured at +20.5% when each field re-dispatched; the row is now read ONCE into a namedtuple, which brings it under the 10% bar. What it buys is that a dict-fed ledger no longer folds 249 rows into one empty event

measurement_note: corroboration is measured with each event's OWN accounts. Passing the whole 249-row ledger to every event costs 41 SECONDS — 9.6M pairwise classifications — which is a benchmark error and not a code defect. Recorded so the next wave does not rediscover it as a regression
